items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: I saw that man in Chicago, playing with Erskine Tate

ctx.x: And they got something from Pops. That was their idol. Now, I don't care how fast Dizzy can get over his instrument and the rest of them. Of course, I caught that

great tribute to Roy Eldridge, 101 hours, I think, stayed up and listened to it, whatever I'd get tired I'd fall when (inaudible) falling asleep. But Jonah Jones, there's some Louie Armstrong in him, Dizzy, Roy Eldridge and just many, many more. That was their idol. I saw that man in Chicago, playing with Erskine Tate -- Carroll Dickinson Dickinson, that's the name, Carroll Dickinson at the Savoy in Chicago.

We drove all the way from Memphis to Chicago, Jimmie Lunsford Lunsford, myself and a few other fellows of the Lunsford Lunsford group to catch Louis Armstrong. He was a ball of fire. He had great personality, big, beautiful smile and playing that trumpet. I'm telling you. He was on the order of King Oliver. That was his idol, King Oliver, and he naturally was an idol of so many other modern day trumpet players and guys that came along. From my beginning I always wanted to hear Louis Armstrong, and that man…
